root_cause.text: The early kernel page table page allocation (EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES) was insufficient because it did not account for the extra page-table page required by the additional early-only mapping split of the [_text, _stext) region (introduced by commit 5973a62efa34), causing the final kernel data segment to overflow into the gap page before early_init_stack.
root_cause.evidence: Commit log explains "since commit 5973a62efa34 ... the early mapper also maps [_text, _stext) separately from [_stext, _etext). This adds one more early-only split and can require one more page-table page than the existing EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES allowance reserves." Patch diff increases EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES from (KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 1) to (KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 2). Crash output shows virtual address ffffffed00601000 (within [data, end)) mapped to physical page that is actually the gap page before early_init_stack, indicating overflow.

candidates.rationale: This constant defines the number of kernel segments, which is used in the calculation of EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES. Its value (5) is insufficient because it does not account for an additional early-only mapping split, leading to a page-table page shortage.

This macro directly computes the number of extra pages for early segment mapping. The formula (KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT + 1) is insufficient because it omits the extra page-table page needed for the split of the [_text, _stext) region, causing kernel data overflow.

vuln_statements.explanation: This macro computes the number of extra pages for early segment mapping. Using KERNEL_SEGMENT_COUNT (5) plus one yields only 6 pages, which is insufficient because the additional early-only mapping split of the [_text, _stext) region requires an extra page-table page. This shortage causes the final kernel data segment to overflow into the gap page before early_init_stack.

This constant defines the number of kernel segments as 5, which does not account for the extra segment split introduced by commit 5973a62efa34. As a result, the derived EARLY_SEGMENT_EXTRA_PAGES is one page short, leading to the page table allocation deficiency described in the root cause.
